title: While Loop with Break/Continue via Exception Signals
description: AST nodes: Num, Var, BinOp, While, Block, Assign, Print, Break, Continue. BreakSignal and ContinueSignal exceptions implement break/continue. While executor: while truthy(cond): try execute(body); except ContinueSignal: continue (re-evaluate cond); except BreakSignal: break (exit loop). Test program: n=7; while n<=50: print n; n=n+7; break. Prints 7 only.

steps.description: AST node classes using dataclass: Num, Var, BinOp, While, Block, Assign, Print, Break, Continue. Each captures its components.
Custom exception classes: BreakSignal and ContinueSignal. Empty classes used as control-flow signals.
truthy helper: numbers false if 0, else bool(value).
evaluate: Num returns value. Var looks up in env (default 0). BinOp evaluates both sides, dispatches on op via dict of lambdas (+, -, *, /, comparisons returning 1.0/0.0).

execute: Assign updates env. Print evaluates and prints. Block executes each statement in order. Break raises BreakSignal. Continue raises ContinueSignal. While: while truthy(evaluate(cond)): try execute(body); except ContinueSignal: continue (loops to condition); except BreakSignal: break (exits loop).

While executor: condition checked before each iteration. ContinueSignal caught -> Python continue re-evaluates condition. BreakSignal caught -> Python break exits while loop. Exception-based control flow.

steps.question: Why use exception classes instead of a boolean flag for break/continue?
steps.answer: Exceptions unwind the call stack automatically through nested Blocks and function calls. A flag would require every execute call to check and propagate it manually. Exceptions handle arbitrary nesting depth without extra code.

steps.description: Test program: env={}. Block: Assign n=7, While n<=50: Block(Print n, Assign n=n+7, Break()). Execute prints 'First multiple of 7:' then 7. Break exits after first iteration.
Output: First multiple of 7: 7 (loop runs once, Break exits)
